quote: and then he goes to dinner and comes back the following Thursday and is fine
why: three coordinating "and"s give a sequence of unequal actions the same flat grammatical weight, the exact chaining pattern the rule bans
suggestion: before going to dinner; he comes back the following Thursday fine.

rule_name: 8. Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Interiority of non-POV characters)
quote: without stopping to think about it, because she is a year older than he is and has not read the paper
why: the narrator asserts Marek's internal deliberative process and his private reasoning, which is interiority of a character other than the POV character
suggestion: He says no before she has finished asking, and goes back to the paper.

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: German is the easiest language anybody has put in front of her.
why: the sentence's entire content is a bare ranking verdict, with the supporting evidence arriving only afterward instead of the verdict following from stated facts
suggestion: German folds onto the Latin she already has, and most of what isn't Latin she can reach sideways through French.

why: a newly built, writerly comparison placed in narration rather than in a character's mouth or thought
suggestion: the vocabulary that isn't Latin is close enough to English that she barely has to translate it

rule_name: Undercut the Achievement in the Same Breath
quote: That is as much as she ever hears about it.
why: the nineteen-day investigation gets a full paragraph of its own as achievement, and the deflating non-reception arrives only in the next paragraph instead of the same breath, letting the reader weigh the two facts separately
suggestion: fold the deflation into the discovery paragraph itself, e.g. end it with "Somebody stopped and never said so, and nobody above Sanders reads past the first page of why."

rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
quote: She spends nineteen days on it
why: exact-duration counting applied by the narration to a scene with no anxiety, control, or dissociation payoff, using the tic as reflexive default rather than as signal
suggestion: She works through the logs, two tables of them, until the pattern gives.

rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
quote: talks her through it for twenty minutes
why: another instance of the narration naming an exact duration as background texture, unattached to any character-specific meaning, the drift the rule warns against
suggestion: talks her through it, unhurried, until she has it

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
why: a universal vague duration marker from the same banned family as "for a second" / "for a while", used regardless of what kind of moment is being timed
suggestion: Make it noisy for a shift change and that's a camera being a camera.

rule_name: Inhabit the Subject, and Give the Reader One Line of It
quote: Formal epistemology is the room four other subjects have been standing outside.
why: this is verbatim the rulebook's own example of going too far: an academic register defining a field in narration instead of showing the accumulated experience through concrete moments
suggestion: cut the framing sentence and open on a concrete problem instead, e.g. "Formal epistemology's first problem set asks her to say what she is entitled to believe, and she cannot answer it in one line."

why: personifying an academic subject as an interrogator is a newly built writerly figure delivered in narration, not in a character's mouth
suggestion: cut the personified chain and let Chloe voice the connection herself, or drop it entirely

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
quote: You went left again, and you went left last time as well.
why: opens a four-turn exchange (lines 97, 99, 101, 103) carrying only one attribution/action beat, at the very end, the same unbroken four-line-one-tag pattern the rule names as the failure case
suggestion: give the middle an anchor, e.g. "Chloe pushes a counter forward. 'I went left because you'd worked out I go left, so left was the surprise.'"

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
why: opens a four-turn exchange (lines 13, 15, 17, 19) with only one tag arriving at the last line, matching the rule's own banned four-turn/one-tag example
suggestion: add a small beat partway through, e.g. '"Why, though?" Marek does not look up from the desk.'

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
why: a bare verdict on the value of Sam's contribution with no evidence of what he actually said, a ranking word standing in for a reason
suggestion: and once talks Odile out of pouring the water jug over the napkin

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: Chloe hears about half of it as an accusation
why: routes Nadia's tone through the perception verb "hears" instead of rendering what specifically makes it land as an accusation
suggestion: Half of what Nadia says lands flat, aimed like an accusation.
